# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_018_page_001.jpg

---

**1** But for your holy ones there was a blazing abundance of light. The Egyptians heard the Israelites' voices in the dark but could not see their faces — and since they themselves were not suffering the same things, they called the Israelites fortunate.

**2** The Israelites had been wronged and had not struck back; now they were grateful for that. And they begged forgiveness for the enmity that had existed between them.

**3** In place of the darkness, you gave your people a pillar of blazing fire — a guide through the unknown journey ahead, a harmless sun to light their glorious march into freedom.

**4** The Egyptians deserved to be stripped of light and imprisoned in darkness — for they had locked away your sons, the people through whom the undying light of the law was meant to be given to the world.

**5** They had plotted to murder the Hebrew infants. One child was exposed and rescued — and in response, as a judgment upon them, you took away a vast number of their children, sweeping them all away together in a mighty flood.

**6** That night was declared to our fathers beforehand, so that knowing clearly what promises they had trusted, they could face it with courage.

**7** So the expectation of your people was this: salvation for the righteous, destruction for their enemies.

**8** The very means by which you struck down our adversaries was the means by which you raised us up with glory when you called us out.

**9** In secret, the holy children of righteous men offered sacrifice and sealed with one voice the divine covenant — that the saints would share equally in good things and in dangers alike. And already they were lifting the praises of the fathers.

**10** Back came the clashing dissonant cry of the enemies — and a sound of pitiful wailing for children spread through every Egyptian house.

**11** Slave and master — punished the same. Commoner and king — the same loss.

**12** In one single form of death, uncountable dead. And the living were not enough to bury them — for at one stroke, the finest generation of that people had been wiped out.

**13** All their sorceries had made them skeptical of everything. But when the firstborn died, they were forced to confess: this people is the son of God.

**14** It was during gentle silence — when all things lay wrapped in stillness, when the night had reached the midpoint of its swift racing course —

**15** that your all-powerful Word came leaping from heaven, from the royal throne. A remorseless warrior, it plunged into the heart of a doomed land,

**16** carrying your irrevocable sentence like a sharp sword. It touched the sky and stood upon the earth, and it filled everything with death.

**17** Then all at once, nightmarish visions threw them into frenzied panic, and fears they had never expected came crashing over them.

**18** One here, another there — they collapsed, half-dead, and as they lay dying they made the reason plain enough —

**19** for the terrifying dreams had warned them exactly what was coming, so that they would not die without knowing the reason for their suffering.

**20** Even the righteous were touched by death's experience — a plague swept through the multitude in the desert. But the wrath did not linger.

**21** For a blameless man leaped to their defence, wielding the particular weapons of his ministry — prayer and the incense that makes atonement. He stood against the wrath and put an end to the disaster, showing himself to be your servant.

**22** He overpowered the wrath — not with physical strength, not with military force. It was by his word that he mastered the one carrying out the punishment: he called upon the oaths and covenants sworn to the fathers.

**23** The dead were already piling up, one upon another. He stepped into the gap, restrained the wrath, and cut off the road to the living.

**24** For on his long ceremonial robe the whole cosmos was depicted — the four rows of precious stones bore the glory of the patriarchs on them, and your own majesty was blazoned on the crown upon his head.

**25** Before these the Destroyer yielded. Before these he shrank back in fear. For it was enough simply to make trial of the wrath with these things alone.
